_comment: Format example for the demo script. language: en or ko, the Pipe's screen language; system_prompt: the instruction both models share; both are written into the Pipe valves by scripts/load_scenario.py. sessions: past chats loaded into Open WebUI and MemMachine with the given date; turns alternate user/assistant and are one minute apart. demos: one topic per recording, with the first question asked verbatim to the no-memory model and then to the memory model in a new chat, and follow_ups to choose from by the condition in 'if'. Every string in expected must appear in the top-k memories retrieved for that question (checked by scripts/demo_check.py). Dates carry the display device's time zone offset. The real scripts are script_en.json and script_ko.json.
system_prompt: You are a helpful assistant. Keep every answer under 80 words, plain and concrete. Answer from what you know. Only when something essential is missing, say so in one sentence and ask one question.

turns.content: My daughter Chloe has a peanut allergy, so we keep the house peanut-free. Can you suggest a few school lunch ideas for her?
Of course. Keeping everything peanut-free: kimbap without peanut sauce, egg rolls with rice, and pasta salad with mozzarella and cucumber.
Chloe loves all kinds of fruit, but she refuses cherries.
Noted: no peanuts and no cherries. I will keep both out of every suggestion for Chloe.
Chloe turns 7 in January and she is obsessed with Frozen right now. Any ideas for her birthday party?
A Frozen party would suit her: a snowflake hunt, party food with winter names, and a paper crown for each guest.
Chloe has a swimming lesson every Saturday morning, so anything for her on a Saturday has to start after lunch.
Good to know. Saturday plans for Chloe start in the afternoon.

first.text: Can you plan the food for Chloe's party this Saturday?
first.why: needs the allergy (chat 1) and the Frozen theme (chat 2)
first.no_memory: asks who Chloe is or lists a generic children's menu

follow_ups.if: the first answer did not say when to start
follow_ups.text: What time should the party start?
